title: Streaming request hang unblock and transactional replay-safe patch
creator: Avery Chen
description: Multiple enterprise customers reported intermittent streaming RPCs that enter a hung state and later surface as 5xx/timeouts when the client retries. Investigation shows a small percentage of long-lived streaming sessions were left in a half-closed state on the serving tier after a kernel-level keepalive race; subsequent retries reused the same request fingerprint which caused duplicate in-flight work and backpressure that produced tenant-visible 5xx spikes. This ticket implements a short-term safe-unblock patch and a replay-safe idempotency shim while we roll out a long-term kernel scheduler and KV-cache eviction fix.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use demo client with streaming enablement and aggressive client-side retry (maxRetries=3, jitter=false)
2) Start ~120 concurrent streams against a staging hosted node, inject a mid-stream TCP RST at ~30-60s for a subset of connections
3) Immediately retry the same logical request with identical fingerprint from the same client, observe one of the original server stream goroutines remain in CLOSE_WAIT for ~15s
4) Repeat until backend latency increases and 5xx responses appear for subsequent requests
investigation_summary: Trace correlation showed requests that became stuck had a mismatch between edge socket lifecycle and runtime stream lifecycle. The runtime's stream admission path failed to clear the request fingerprint on connection termination in a narrow race when TCP FIN and upstream kernel timer occurred simultaneously. This allowed retries to be treated as in-flight duplicates and blocked new work on a per-tenant admission semaphore, which cascaded to 5xx when semaphores saturated.
root_cause: Edge connection teardown races with runtime stream finalizers leaving request fingerprint entries and holding admission semaphores. Retries reuse the fingerprint, leading to duplicate hold and admission starvation under load.
mitigation_plan: Hotpatch (short-term): Add a connection-finalizer hook that forcibly clears request fingerprints synchronously on socket close to avoid stale entries (safe and reversible).

Idempotency shim (short-term): Accept logically duplicate requests if their prior in-flight entry is older than 10s and incrementally fast-fail to client with Retry-After header rather than blocking admission.
Observability (short-term): Add a streaming-fingerprint-age metric and a tenant-admission-wait histogram to Grafana dashboards and alert when >2% of admissions exceed 5s.
Long-term: Revise kernel scheduler and KV-cache eviction to make fingerprint removal fully atomic with stream lifecycle, and add admission-burst buffer to avoid semaphore exhaustion.
implementation_notes: Patch implemented in two commits: a synchronous finalizer in runtime/stream/conn_finalizer.go and a guarded idempotency fallback path in runtime/edge/admission.go. Local unit tests added for connection race scenario; load test harness updated to simulate FIN+timer race. New config flags: streaming.fingerprint_grace_seconds (default 10) and admission.fastfail_threshold_ms (default 5000).

acceptance_criteria: Hotpatch deployed to 100% of hosted nodes with no regressions for 48h
Grafana alert for admission wait reduced to <0.5% above 5s over 24h window
Customers A and B confirm no new 5xx incidents related to streaming hangs for two business days
Integration tests covering FIN+timer race pass in CI and are added to nightly stress suite
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Synchronous finalizer could add a small CPU latency on connection close under extreme connection churn. Mitigation: limit finalizer work to O(1) fingerprint removal and run microbenchmarks; provide rollout knob streaming.finalizer_rate_limit.
Risk: Idempotency shim may mask legitimate duplicate submissions. Mitigation: conservative default grace window (10s) and telemetry for dedup decisions so PM can tune after rollout.

Risk: Rollout may interact with Dedicated/private runtime versions. Mitigation: coordinate with Platform Release for a staged deploy across Dedicated and Private channels and add compatibility gate in console for customers running older runtime versions.
